label: early original-phase token after a prefix made only of 3/f/z/0/x
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (99% of mass) at early positions t=2-5 (t=2,3 hold 79% of mass), and never at t=0 or 1. It depends on which tokens came before: the previous and second-previous inputs are strongly enriched for f, z, 0, 3 and x (lift 5-10x), and the first token is often 3 (14x lift, 49% of mass). The current input is enriched for r, x, h, o, 3, 2, d. The strongest examples look like 3 z z [x], 3 f z [x] and 3 3 f z [r]: a run of these tokens followed by r/x/h/o. Weaker activations come from looser versions of this pattern. It almost never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase. The predicate (every earlier token in {3,f,z,0,x} and the current token in the enriched set) reaches only about 0.39 F1 on dev. The feature looks like a graded, weighted mix of prefix-token identities rather than a clean boolean rule.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=f (+5.92), prev2_tok=f (+5.47), orig0=3 (+5.34), prev_tok=z (+4.51), orig0=v (+4.44), prev2_tok=x (+4.17). Lower it: in_tok=g (-4.20), in_tok=p (-4.08), in_tok=w (-3.96), orig2=u (-3.79).
